newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate plunges at close on demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate plunges at close on demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates fell 135 basis points to close at 17.40 percent on demand for paper ahead of the forthcoming long weekend, traders said.
"Many who were short paper stepped in to cover, and the dollar was at a good rate for switching to pesos to cover those shorts," a trader said.
Mexican financial markets will close for Labor Day on Thursday, and for the anniversary of the battle of Puebla on Monday, May 5.
Other traders said overnight rates fell in line with U.S. long bond yields.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 10/32 in late trade to yield 6.96 percent.
"The long bond did well despite strong U.S. GDP data, and the peso was also stable," another trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed just 0.9 of a centavo weaker at 7.7.9500/7.9520 per dollar.
Traders said central bank intervention also set the stage for low overnight rates.
Banco de Mexico drained 863 million pesos from the system through three direct Cetes sales combined with one repo.
"Banco de Mexico assigned its repo at a low rate, and secondary rates began to fall from then on," a trader said. The central bank assigned the repo overnight at 17.95 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 25 basis points at 19.25 percent.
June contracts for Cetes futures traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange ended up 25 centavos at 77.99 pesos.
Liquidity of 1.552 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank operations.
